findings.title: Light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 70% for embedded post author links
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme branch now uses 70% instead of 30%, so these author names become much paler on light themes. The values look swapped; following the pattern used everywhere else, it should be `(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Light-theme lightness changed from 70% to 30% for custom-message-length
findings.body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The arguments are inverted, so on light themes the hint text becomes much darker than before. It should be `(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, matching the desktop modal.scss change.

findings.title: Topic-map h3 light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: On mobile, the `.topic-map h3` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. It became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This alters the light-theme appearance, which a dark-theme-only fix should not do, and it diverges from the desktop rule. It should be `(20%, 80%)`.

findings.title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50% on light themes
findings.body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the replacement uses 50% for the light branch and 50% for the dark branch. As a result, member names are lighter than before on light themes and look the same as `.title`. To preserve the existing light-theme look, the call should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50% on light themes (mobile)
findings.body: This is the same issue as on desktop. The original 30% lightness was replaced with `dark-light-choose(50%, 50%)`, which unintentionally lightens member names on light themes. It should be `(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.
